# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`
data.title: Limiter skip log prints 10/7 when the reserve is in use

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.
data.title: Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want the client-side bridge to log one line per
captured compaction signal and one line per reshape attempt, so that a
loaded-but-idle extension (bridge installed, no signal ever arrives) is
distinguishable from a broken one (signal arrived, bridge did nothing) —
satisfying AC4's client half and making the parent's pass criterion D
(ordering evidence) observable.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — required whether or not Phase B
passes.

## Cross-repo constraint (read first)

This work lands in the **SorraAgents** repository, not this one:

- code: `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`
  (`index.ts` adapter + `compaction-bridge.js` pure core),
- tests: `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
- loaded via the symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` →
  that directory (verified present 2026-10-31), so no reinstall is needed
  beyond `/reload` inside pi.

The commit hash in SorraAgents must be recorded on this child and on the
parent, so the client half of AC4 is traceable from the LP item. Do not copy
the bridge into this repository.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `compaction-bridge.js` has no logging at all: `handleResponse` returns a
  boolean, `reshape` returns a list or `null`. Neither reports why.
- `index.ts` wires `after_provider_response` and `context` and silently
  returns on a stale ctx / missing signal.
- There is no `ctx.ui` in print or JSON mode (`docs/extensions.md`), so
  `ctx.ui.notify` cannot be the logging channel — headless T2 would lose it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: One line per **captured** signal, emitted from the pure core:
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`.
- AC2: One line per **reshape attempt**:
  - applied: `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=<id8>`
    with `Y < X`,
  - not applicable: `compaction-bridge no signal — passthrough session=<id8>`
    (state absent) — the "loaded but idle" line, and
  - anomalous signal (fewer turns than `turnsSummarized`):
    `compaction-bridge reshape refused reason=insufficient_turns session=<id8>`.
- AC3: Exactly one line per event: `handleResponse` logs once whether or not a
  signal was parsed (no-signal case logs at most once per response, and is
  rate-limited to one line per session per turn so an idle session does not
  spam), and `reshape` logs once per `context` event.
- AC4: Works in every pi mode (interactive, RPC, JSON, print): no `ctx.ui`
  dependency. Lines go to **stderr** and, when
  `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG` is set, are appended to that file, one line
  each. The default channel and the optional file path are documented in the
  extension README.
- AC5: No marker text, no message content and no summary body in any line —
  session id (truncated to 8), counts and lengths only.
- AC6: Logging never changes behaviour and never throws: the logger is
  injected into `createCompactionBridge({ log })` with a no-op default, so the
  pure module stays dependency-free and a hostile/throwing logger leaves
  parse/reshape results identical.
- AC7: `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended to assert: the AC1 line
  and its fields; the AC2 applied / passthrough / refused lines; the AC3
  one-line-per-event rule including the idle no-spam case; the AC5 no-body
  guarantee (assert the marker string does not appear in any captured line);
  and AC6 (identical `parseCompactionSignal` / `reshapeContext` results with a
  no-op logger vs a throwing logger). All pre-existing bridge tests stay green
  unmodified.
- AC8: README documents the exact log lines, the `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG`
  variable, and the grep recipe used by T2's criterion D.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `log` option to `createCompactionBridge({ log } = {})` defaulting to a
  no-op; the default writer lives in `index.ts` (adapter layer), keeping
  `compaction-bridge.js` free of `fs`/`process` imports except behind an
  injected function.
- Emit from inside `handleResponse` / `reshape` where the decision is already
  made — no re-parsing, no extra state.
- Idle rate-limiting is one `Set` of session ids already logged for
  passthrough, cleared when a signal is captured for that session (keeps the
  module dependency-free and the logic pure).
- Keep the existing public surface (`handleResponse` boolean, `reshape` list or
  null) unchanged so `index.ts` and the tests need no behavioural edits.
- Run `node --test` for the extension's unit test only via the test skill
  (`/skill:test` scope) — not ad-hoc.

## Deliverables

- `compaction-bridge.js` telemetry + injected logger.
- `index.ts` default logger wiring (stderr + optional file).
- `README.md` log-line documentation.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended coverage.
- SorraAgents commit hash recorded on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T2 execution child (pass criterion D reads these lines).
data.title: Bridge telemetry: signal-captured and reshape log lines (SorraAgents)

# Regression fence: router-mode `/slots` model param must yield live detail

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7 (router-mode `/slots` observability regression).
Slice 1 of 5 — **test-first**, before any production change.

## Why this is first

The model-parameter path (`?model=`) and child-port discovery were both
implemented after the 2026-11-04 incident (LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW,
LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, LP-0MVWBXEAI008YZ7B), but there is **no single
end-to-end fixture** proving the contract the incident broke: a router-mode
server that answers `400` to model-less `/slots` and slot detail to
`/slots?model=<id>`. The existing tests fence pieces
(`test_slots_model_param_guard.py` scans call sites;
`test_slots_model_id_resolution.py` resolves ids;
`test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` rotates ports) but nothing asserts
the composed behaviour: *the proxy obtains detail and does not fall back to
a snapshot.*

This item is the tracer bullet: it pins the AC1 contract with a test that
fails loudly if `?model=` is ever dropped again, and it proves the incident
root cause is closed before slices 2-4 add new behaviour on top.

## Scope

**New file** `proxy/tests/test_slots_router_mode_detail.py`:

1. A fake llama-server router fixture where `GET /slots` (no `model`) returns
   `400 {"error":{"code":400,"message":"model name is missing from the request"}}`
   and `GET /slots?model=<id>` returns a 2-slot detail list.
2. Assert `GET /llama/local/status` against that fixture returns the live
   detail: `slots` has 2 entries with the fixture's `slot_id`s,
   `slots_detail_stale` is `false`, `slot_counts_stale` is `false`, and
   `slots_snapshot_source` is **not** `"snapshot"`.
3. Assert a *second* poll still shows the same slot identities (no fossil
   swap-in) and that the upstream call count is non-zero.
4. Assert the router-mode child-port preference: when a discoverable child
   port exists, the `/slots` request goes to the child port, and the
   `no_child_port_router_mode` fallback counter does not increment.
5. Assert the negative control: with `/slots?model=` also broken (400), the
   payload reports `slots_detail_stale: true` and a snapshot source — i.e.
   the test genuinely distinguishes the two regimes and is not vacuous.

Reuse `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` and the status-handler test harness used
by `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`; do not build a second
harness.

If any assertion fails against current `dev`, the fix belongs in this item —
the fence must be green, not marked `xfail`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Against a router-mode llama-server fixture (`role: router`,
      `models_autoload: true`) where `/slots` without `model` returns 400 and
      with `model` returns slot detail, the proxy obtains per-slot detail and
      does not fall back to a snapshot.
- [ ] The detail assertion checks the fixture's `slot_id`s with
      `slots_detail_stale=false` and `slots_snapshot_source != "snapshot"`.
- [ ] A negative-control assertion proves the test distinguishes a working
      `?model=` path from a failing one (the failing control yields
      `slots_detail_stale=true`).
- [ ] The test asserts the child-port preference and that the
      `no_child_port_router_mode` fallback is not taken when a child port is
      discoverable.
- [ ] No production behaviour is changed by this slice (test-only); the
      changed-scope gate passes.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_router_mode_detail.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` (reuse fixtures)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py` (reuse harness patterns)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (read-only reference: `_query_slots`,
  `_query_slots_detail`)
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (read-only reference: `get_llama_local_status`)

## Dependencies

None. Blocks slices 2-5.

## Notes

- Do not restate or duplicate `test_slots_model_param_guard.py`'s static
  call-site scan; this item is about composed runtime behaviour.
- If the fixture needs a real port, bind `:0` and use the existing
  `httpx` mock-client injection points (`_client=` / `base_url=`) rather than
  opening sockets — the suite must stay offline and fast.
data.title: Regression fence: router-mode /slots model param yields live detail

data.comment: Scope boundary with LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7 (router-mode /slots observability regression), planned into 5 slices. Slice 3 there adds `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` so a snapshot older than the ceiling stops being presented as a live slot list, and stops availability being claimed from a too-old snapshot. That item does NOT touch the fresh-data case: `available_slots` contradicting its own `slots[]` when both are fresh remains this item's scope. No duplication; the two are complementary halves of the 2026-11-04 incident.
